verdict.line: You lose if you auto into a ready Riposte or get poked down by double Lunge before level 6; you win if you survive to your item spikes and force extended trades.

brief.thesis: This is a 46.9% matchup over 1472 games because both champions win different phases: Fiora's Q (Lunge) can dash twice in a short window to poke and reset neutral, while K'Sante's Q (Ntofo Strikes) builds toward a 2-stack shockwave that pulls her into forced extended trades where his kit and itemization take over. Whoever controls when the fight actually starts wins the lane.

theirWindow.when: E (Burst of Speed) active and stacking
theirWindow.what: She's gaining Attack Speed and stacking Move Speed off every landed attack or Lunge. Don't try to disengage on foot during this window — use E (Footwork) to shield and reposition instead of walking away.

yourWindow.what: The shockwave pulls her in regardless of any dash she just used. Bait her W (Riposte) with a Q poke first, then commit the real trade once it's down — Riposte only blocks one basic attack, not your abilities.

start.why: Highest pick rate (76%) and win rate (45.4%) start in this matchup over 1330 games — the sustain and regen offset Fiora's passive healing poke better than raw shield value early.

boots.why: 85% pick rate at 45% win rate — Fiora is a pure physical-damage autoattacker, and the flat reduction blunts both her Lunge hits and her E-empowered attack speed window.

core.why: Directly counters her Duelist passive healing stacks before she can snowball a trade
Adds the slow and wave clear needed to punish her dash-ins without overextending
Highest-sample core path (54.4% win rate over 90 games) — grievous wounds shuts down her sustain entirely
Completes the tank spike that defines your level 11-18 power curve advantage

their comp adds meaningful AP damage alongside Fiora

runes.keystoneWhy: Rewards the extended trades you're forcing with your 2-stack Q pull, and the attached healing fights directly against her Duelist stacking.

summoners.why: Flash+Teleport is run in 71.4% of games at 44.5% win rate — Teleport lets you reset after losing early poke exchanges and still make clutch plays once your item spikes online. Flash+Ignite (24.2% pick, 49.2% win rate) is the stronger pick if you're confident you can land your Q shockwave pull for a level 2-3 kill window.

playing.title: Bait Riposte before committing
playing.detail: Throw a Q poke or let her shield block a non-essential hit first. Riposte only reflects one basic attack, so your abilities go through regardless — but a wasted auto into an active parry costs you the whole trade.

playing.title: Track her double Lunge
playing.detail: Her Q (Lunge) can be used twice within a couple seconds at no mana cost. If she dashes in once, expect the second hit immediately — don't relax after the first.

playing.title: Hold W for the charge-up mitigation
playing.detail: W (Path Maker) reduces damage taken while charging before the dash. Use the charge window itself to eat a Lunge or an E-empowered auto, then release into the knockback stun.

playing.title: Force fights after 2 Q stacks
playing.detail: The shockwave pull on your second Q stack cancels her spacing entirely. This is your primary engage tool before level 6 — use it to start trades, not just to punish hers.

playing.title: Respect her E speed stacking
playing.detail: Once Burst of Speed is active, every landed attack or Lunge adds more Move Speed. If you can't finish the trade in the first two exchanges, disengage with E (Footwork) rather than trying to outrun her on foot.

playing.title: Rush Bramble Vest first
playing.detail: Her Duelist passive stacks healing off every hit she lands on you. Getting grievous wounds online early is worth more than raw damage items against her sustain.

playing.title: Save R for a wall
playing.detail: All Out knocks her through any wall in the path before you transform. Fight near lane walls or jungle terrain so the knockback actually displaces her instead of just repositioning her in open space.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, summoners, and all win rates above are measured from real games on the current patch via OP.GG; the trade-pattern and timing analysis is my own read on why those numbers shake out this way.
